title: Public confessions: Thorun Polish Declaration and English Confession on saving faith
source_text: XV. Sed omissis aliis privatorum doctorum definitionibus, hic maxime considerandae sunt fidei descriptiones quae publice Ecclesiarum Reformatarum Confessionibus sunt veluti sancitae. Qualis est illa quae habetur in Declaratione doctrinae Catholicae Ecclesiarum Reformatarum, in conventu Thoruniensi, ab Ecclesiarum Polonicarum deputatis lecta & exhibita, Anno 1645. Et in Confessione Ecclesiae Anglicanae, Parliamenti, ut vocant, Anglicani, circa idem tempus, jussu & mandato publicata. Et Ecclesiae quidem Polonicae, Declarationis suae capite quarto, paragrapho octavo, sic suam de fide sententiam exponunt. Veram autem fidem & justificantem eam demum dicimus, qua promissionem Evangelii, qua resipiscentibus remissio & vita in Christo offertur, assensu practico seu fiduciali amplectitur, & corde vere contrito sibi applicat, quaque deinceps per charitatem est efficax: cap. 4. sect. 1. num. 8. Illa vero, quam diximus Anglicana Confessio sic describit fidem salutarem, Per hanc fidem Christianus verum credit quicquid est verbo Dei revelatum, propter Dei ipsius in verbo loquentis authoritatem, & differenter agit ac afficitur super singula quae continet istud verbum; mandatis scilicet, obsequens, ad minas contremiscens, & amplectens Dei promissiones, tam quae ad hanc vitam, quam quae ad futuram pertinent. Sed praecipua Acta salutaris illius fidei sunt acceptare & recipere Christum, & in eo solo acquiescere ad justificationem, & vitam aeternam, virtute foederis gratiae: cap. 14.
pass_a_gloss: But omitting other definitions of private doctors, here those descriptions of faith are especially to be considered which are as it were sanctioned publicly by the Confessions of the Reformed Churches. Such is that which is had in the Declaration of the Catholic doctrine of the Reformed Churches, in the assembly at Toruń, read and exhibited by the deputies of the Polish Churches, in the year 1645. And in the Confession of the English Church, published by order and mandate of the English Parliament, as they call it, about the same time. And the Polish Church indeed, in the eighth paragraph of the fourth chapter of its Declaration, thus sets out its mind on faith. But we call that at last true and justifying faith by which the promise of the Gospel, by which remission and life in Christ are offered to those who repent, is embraced with practical or fiducial assent, and applied to oneself with a truly contrite heart, and by which afterward it is efficacious through charity: ch. 4, sect. 1, num. 8. But that English Confession which we mentioned thus describes saving faith: By this faith a Christian believes as true whatever is revealed by the word of God, because of the authority of God Himself speaking in the word, and differently acts and is affected upon the several things which that word contains — obedient to commands, namely, trembling at threats, and embracing God’s promises, both those which pertain to this life and those which pertain to the future. But the chief Acts of that saving faith are to accept and receive Christ, and to rest in Him alone unto justification and eternal life, by the power of the covenant of grace: ch. 14.
pass_b_english: Public Reformed confessions outweigh private doctor lists.
Toruń 1645 Polish Declaration IV.8: justifying faith fiducially embraces and applies the Gospel promise with a contrite heart — then efficacious through charity.
English Confession (~same time) ch. 14: believe all God reveals; obey, tremble, embrace promises.
Chief acts: accept and receive Christ; rest in Him alone for justification and eternal life by the covenant of grace.
